unlinked_requirements_few: {count} requirements name no problem or goal of the need — {ids}
unlinked_requirements_many: {count} requirements name no problem or goal of the need — {ids}
material_title_placeholder: What it is: Interview with an operator, 2026-10-12
material_content_placeholder: Paste the interview, the request or the report as it is.
add_files_title: Markdown, plain text, CSV, HTML, e-mail or subtitles; each file is one material
accept_need_title: Write what was accepted to docs/discovery.md, as a pull request
accept_need_none_title: Accept readings first: only what a person accepted is written
materials_read_note: Materials are read as soon as they are added: on your own model key, else an AI connection you reach — yours, the workspace's or the organization's.
needs_empty_title: No problems, goals or ideas read yet.
needs_empty_body: They come from the project's materials — interviews, requests, a PRD's problem statement — once a build reads them with the current extractor.
needs_howto_body: Who has which problem, what they want to reach and what the materials propose, each with the passage it comes from. Accept or reject each reading; a link nobody stated is shown as a gap, never filled in. What you accept becomes the need, proposed as a document.
gaps_one: {count} gap in the need — a problem nothing solves, an idea with no problem
gaps_few: {count} gaps in the need — a problem nothing solves, an idea with no problem
gaps_many: {count} gaps in the need — a problem nothing solves, an idea with no problem
hyp_empty_body: A hypothesis comes from what someone expects a solution to do for someone — “the search will let operators find a request in seconds” — once a build reads it with the current extractor.
hyp_howto: Check what is expected, not what is written.
hyp_howto_body: Each benefit someone expects is a hypothesis: which solution, for whom, with what effect. Studio proposes how to check it; what the check found is yours to record. Accepting the wording is not validating it, and an unchecked hypothesis stops nothing.
hyp_propose_title: Write every hypothesis, where it stands and how it is checked to docs/hypotheses.md, as a pull request
criterion: Criterion to read a result by
criterion_placeholder: Not agreed: a result is then exploratory
result_placeholder: Paste or write the result: who was observed or asked, under what conditions, what was seen.
exploratory: No criterion agreed: the result is kept as exploratory.
blocked_one: {count} action or scenario a confirmed rule forbids as written
blocked_few: {count} actions or scenarios a confirmed rule forbids as written
blocked_many: {count} actions or scenarios a confirmed rule forbids as written
beh_empty_body: They come from an entity's states (a lifecycle that lists them) and the actions roles take on it, once a build reads them with the current extractor.
beh_howto: What the specification must say about behaviour.
beh_howto_body: For each action roles take on a thing and each state it goes through: may it happen then? A question is answered only where one passage names both; otherwise answer it in the documents, or exclude it with a reason. What a rule you accepted forbids is shown first. None of this blocks a build.
rules_howto: Check the rules against each other.
rules_howto_body: Only rules a member accepted are checked. Each is read into a precise form — who may do what, a number that bounds something — shown so you can say it is what the rule means. Two that cannot both hold are a conflict, shown with both passages.
rules_empty_body: Accept the constraints you agree with on an entity's card; only those are checked, so an unconfirmed reading never becomes a verdict.
